$comment: Every Ruvyxa response carries these unless the application sets its own. The
list exists three times and cannot be shared as code:
A header added to one language and not the other means the same site is
protected differently depending on where it is deployed — and nothing about
a missing response header fails a build or shows up in a log.
Add a header here first; a port that drifts then fails in the language that
drifted rather than silently on one deployment target.
$valueNote: Names are compared case-insensitively — HTTP header names are — but values are compared exactly, because `finalize_security_headers` only strips a header still holding the exact default and a changed value would quietly become unstrippable.
